profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
https://alejandro.pe/

versatile design-minded builder/hacker with experience across startups and large companies in consumer (Airbnb, Pinterest), productivity (YC startup Muddy/Sail), and enterprise (Watershed).

Keywords: Product Engineer, full-stack engineer, frontend engineer, design engineer.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
helped build the first version of the Watershed Agent (https://watershed.com/platform/sustainability-ai), an AI coding agent for sustainability data analysis, working across the agent harness (Claude Code SDK, Modal sandboxes, Temporal) and the product experience. Previously helped launch Watershed Labs, the company's experimental AI product group, where I prototyped and built AI-native tools including copilot-powered dashboards, spreadsheet-style data exploration, and an autonomous agent for navigating data lineage, pitched to leadership, and showed to customers.

Before moving into AI, shipped core product features including interactive data visualizations, emissions calculation pipelines, and large-scale data analysis tools. Championed improvements to the design system, frontend infrastructure, and testing. Mentored teammates on frontend engineering best practices.

In 2025, I was the top Cursor user at Watershed, ranked in the top 0.01% of Cursor users in San Francisco, and voted the "most AI-pilled" person at the company. One coworker once called me "the iconic vibecoder of Watershed."

Watershed is a climate tech company backed by Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins.

Stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, DuckDB/Parquet, Temporal, Modal, Claude Code SDK.

positions.title: Founding Software Engineer
positions.description:
Built a multiplayer web browser for teams on top of Chromium at YC-backed startup ($5.5M seed). Prototyped and built novel browser interfaces and real-time collaboration features, including a multiplayer infinite canvas, messaging, notifications, audio calls, and collaborative text editing (TipTap/ProseMirror).
Worked across the stack, from complex React interfaces to real-time collaboration infrastructure. The browser ran on a custom Chromium fork with a JS/C++ bridge exposing native browser functionality (tabs, rendering, history, extensions, etc.).

We set out to rethink how people use computers together and make a dent in productivity software. Although we gained some early traction, we ultimately struggled to find product-market fit and wound down. I learned a ton along the way about building products from 0 to 1, pushing browser technology, crafting complex frontends, prototyping and talking to users, navigating pivots, and where software might go :)

I wrote a blog post about what I learned building Sail and Muddy, which made the front page of Hacker News:
https://www.alejandro.pe/writing/sail-muddy-lessons

Stack: Chromium, TypeScript, React, Node.js, Redis Pub/Sub, GraphQL Subscriptions, MongoDB.

More details on the projects:
https://alejandro.pe/projects/muddy
https://alejandro.pe/projects/sail
positions.insights: Skills: Cultural Competency · Interactive Web · Amazon Web Services (AWS)

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Built core parts of Airbnb's search experience, contributing to every major search product launch from 2019 to 2022, including Flexible Dates, Flexible Destinations, Airbnb Categories, Online Experiences, nearby destination search during COVID-19, and the 2019 redesign. Worked across the stack, from prototyping new search experiences and building polished consumer interfaces to frontend architecture, search APIs, and backend services.

Tech lead for Flexible Dates search, helping build new ways for travelers to explore Airbnb without fixed dates or destinations. Also built the search experience for "I'm Flexible 2.0" and new category filters, and helped redesign and rewrite much of the search frontend, including autocomplete, date pickers, guest selection, price filters, and mobile search flows.

Contributed to frontend architecture and a TypeScript rewrite of the search filters, participated in the main web app's on-call rotation, and gave an external talk on building flexibility into Airbnb Search.

External talk, "How Airbnb Built Flexibility into Search": https://reengineeringtravel.splashthat.com/

Press:
https://techcrunch.com/2022/05/11/airbnb-categories-split-stays-aircover/
https://www.theverge.com/2022/5/11/23066798/airbnb-lovefrom-jony-ive-redesign-categories-split-stays
https://techcrunch.com/2021/02/24/airbnb-plans-for-a-new-kind-of-travel-post-covid-with-flexible-search/

Stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js, Java, Kubernetes.
positions.insights: Skills: Cultural Competency · Interactive Web · Amazon Web Services (AWS)

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Worked on Airbnb's design system, building polished, reusable React UI components and developer tooling to make building great interfaces faster and easier. Learned a lot about design engineering, UI craftsmanship, and web infrastructure.

Technologies: JavaScript, React, Webpack, Babel (transpiling, codemods, AST parsing etc.), ESLint, Storybook, Happo (visual diffing).

positions.title: Accel Scholar
positions.description:
selected by venture capital firm Accel and UC Berkeley’s EECS department for personalized mentorship, networking, and industry-relevant curriculum. Accel investments include Facebook, Dropbox, Slack, Spotify etc.

https://techcrunch.com/2017/11/01/accel-launches-uc-berkeley-mentorship-program/
https://eecs.berkeley.edu/resources/undergrads/accel

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
As an undergrad I helped with research in the following labs:

- Hybrid Ecologies Lab:
Exploring Augmented Reality for hybrid making and fabrication. Microsoft Hololens (C#, Unity).

- Algorithms for Computing and Education (BiD):
 Helped with the integration of learning program transformation by example algorithms to OK (https://okpy.org/), Berkeley's Automate Grading & Personalize Feedback App. Used Python and C#.

- Berkeley Institute of Data Science (BIDS): 
Developed Data Science Visualization using React.js and Bokeh (JS and Python).

positions.title: Software Engineering Pintern
positions.description:
Worked on Pinterest's design system (Gestalt) and the rewrite of Pinterest's mobile web app as a Progressive Web App (PWA). Built reusable React UI components, ran A/B experiments, and helped rebuild the mobile web experience with a focus on performance and user experience.

Learned a ton about design systems, frontend infrastructure, experimentation, and how platform teams help engineering organizations scale. Also got to see how engineers could rally teams around ambitious technical projects.

Stack: JavaScript, React, Redux, Python (APIs/backend).

Pinterest's React UI library:
https://github.com/pinterest/gestalt
Case study on Pinterest's Progressive Web App:
https://medium.com/dev-channel/a-pinterest-progressive-web-app-performance-case-study-3bd6ed2e6154

positions.title: KPCB Engineering Fellow
positions.description:
Mentorship program by KPCB VC firm. 57 Engineering Fellows  out of ~2500 applicants. http://kpcbfellows.com/

KPCB investments include Google, Amazon, Figma, Snapchat, etc.

positions.title: Software Enginnering Pintern
positions.description:
First "job in Sillicon Valley" after freshman year. Learned a lot about big tech companies and what it takes to scale them. I worked on the Observability Infrastructure team, wrote jobs for Pinterest’s internal analytics dashboard (Python) and wrote realtime ingestion pipeline for “Pintrace” distributed tracer (Spark, Kafka, Thrift, Zipkin). 

Pintrace got open sourced! you can read more about it here:
https://medium.com/pinterest-engineering/distributed-tracing-at-pinterest-with-new-open-source-tools-a4f8a5562f6b

positions.title: Instructor & Web Developer
positions.description:
In my 6 months after graduating high school from Peru and before starting college in the U.S. I worked at Laboratoria, a 6-month bootcamp that empowers people from low-income backgrounds by giving them access to education and work in the digital sector.  I simultaneously worked at "Ayu" a small web dev agency owned by the founders of Laboratoria. At Laboratoria I learned a lot about scaling a startup, web development, education and social impact organizations. 

I was an early employee in Peru (less than 5 employees), today Laboratoria has multiple offices across Latin America (Peru, Mexico, Chile, Brazil, Colombia).  I was a web development instructor in Laboratoria's Bootcamp. As part of my work, I developed coursework, lesson plans, and internal tools for teaching. 

https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-05-05/learning-to-code-empowers-women-in-latin-america

https://www.theguardian.com/global-development-professionals-network/2016/dec/01/cracking-code-tech-women-latin-america-

https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/features/2015/03/peru-code-breaking-women-150308070034951.html

https://blogs.worldbank.org/education/bootcamps-raising-expectations-girls-math-science-and-technology

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description: In my 6 months after graduating high school from Peru, In addition to working at Laboratoria I worked at Ayu, a small web dev agency, owned by the founders of Laboratoria. I learned a lot about  web development and how agencies work and what it's like building projects for a customer.  I worked with HTML, CSS, JS, PHP/MySQL, Codeigniter and the MEAN stack (MongoDB, Express, Angular and Node.js) I also dabbled a bit on UI/UX research and learned about "Design Thinking".

positions.title: Independent iOS Game Developer
positions.description:
naively got into programming by making iPhone games in high school using objective-c and the cocos2d library. I owned the entire process: game design, graphic design, level design and programming.  After pouring many hours working after school and 2 summers I published 3 games for sale on the apple appstore to play on my ipod touch 4. The games were fun enough to play but most importantly they were a lot of fun to make. I programmed, made art, and designed the games myself. The experience gave me a lot of respect for game developers and taught me a lot about picking up new skills and the craftsmanship, joy, and challenge that goes into making something end to end and got me into the career path I am in today.
